title: Label free, quantitative single-cell fate tracking of time-lapse movies
author: Caldon, Burgess

steps.title: Seed cells at appropriate confluency
steps.instruction: Seed adherent cells (e.g., A549, H358, HeLa, Hs578 T, MD‑MB‑231, MCF‑7, MCF10A) at approximately 30 % confluency the day before imaging in a standard plastic 6‑, 12‑, or 24‑well plate.

steps.title: Prepare imaging plate and select fields
steps.instruction: On the day of imaging ensure cells are 40–50 % confluent, place the plate on an inverted live‑cell microscope, and choose 2–3 random fields per well/condition. Use long‑working‑distance 10X or 20X lenses; if higher magnification (>20X) is required, switch to thin optical plastic or glass‑bottom dishes.

steps.title: Configure microscope settings and acquisition interval
steps.instruction: Adjust brightfield, DIC or phase contrast to maximize image quality while minimizing exposure (avoid excessive light, especially fluorescence). Optionally add fluorescent channels such as propidium iodide (1 µg ml⁻¹) to the media for cell‑death detection. Set the image acquisition interval between 5 and 20 min (5 min or less preferred for accurate mitotic length analysis, as a normal mitosis lasts ~20–40 min).

steps.title: Acquire time‑lapse images and import into Fiji
steps.instruction: Capture the time‑lapse sequence on the microscope, then import the files into Fiji via Import > Image Sequence. If memory is limited, enable ‘use virtual stack’, convert to greyscale, and/or skip unnecessary frames to reduce file size.

steps.title: Set spatial and temporal scale in Fiji
steps.instruction: Open Image > Properties…; if the unit of length is ‘pixel’, determine the pixel‑to‑micron conversion using a calibration slide and enter the value in the Width field (Height and Depth auto‑populate, unit changes to ‘micron’). Optionally input the time‑frame interval (t) in the same dialog.

steps.title: Add scale bar and time counter
steps.instruction: Insert a scale bar via Analyze > Tools > Scale Bar…, set desired length, choose ‘overlay’ so it appears on all frames (or draw a line where you want the bar first). Add a time counter via Image > Stacks > Label…, select the format and interval length, then click OK.

steps.title: Correct uneven lighting and save movie
steps.instruction: Apply Bleach Correction (Image > Adjust > Bleach Correction), select ‘Simple Ratio’, keep background intensity at 0.0 (increase to 1 or higher only if needed). Save the processed movie as a .tiff (or as .avi at 30 fps for presentations). If using Photoshop CC, convert .avi to .mp4 (H.264) beforehand because newer Photoshop versions may not read .avi correctly.

steps.title: Identify mitotic and death events in movies
steps.instruction: Using the processed movie, score mitotic length from nuclear envelope breakdown (NEBD) to anaphase. NEBD is indicated by loss of nuclear envelope, loss of nucleoli, and/or cell rounding; anaphase by chromatid separation and a ‘figure‑8’ membrane invagination. If intervals >5 min are used, note that some phases may be missed and record the first frame after the event. Optionally score cytokinesis (breakage of the cytoplasmic bridge) and cell death (loss of nuclear envelope, nucleoli, detachment, floating, membrane ruffling/blebbing). Propidium iodide fluorescence can aid death identification.

steps.title: Track individual cells with Fiji multi‑point tool
steps.instruction: Open the saved .tiff, enable the multi‑point tool (right‑click the point tool), click the first cell of interest (labelled #1) and follow it through the time‑course until NEBD, anaphase, or death occurs. Record the times in an Excel sheet. Continue tracking the same cell for any observed mitotic phenotypes, then optionally follow one random daughter cell. Return to frame one, select another cell (#2), and repeat until 50–100 cells have been analyzed (≈25–50 cells hour⁻¹). Save the .tiff after labeling to preserve the points.

steps.title: Record event times in Excel template
steps.instruction: Open the supplied Excel movie template (Supplementary File S1). Delete the demo data in columns B–K. Duplicate the Condition #1 and Fate Map #1 sheets for each experimental condition. (Optional) add extra grand‑daughter columns for long movies (3–5 days). For each tracked cell, enter NEBD, anaphase, death times and any phenotypes in Row 3 of the corresponding sheet. Update the running total list of phenotypes as you go.

steps.title: Process Excel data and generate fate maps
steps.instruction: After all cells are entered, edit columns M‑Q as instructed. In Q3, replace the formula with one that reflects the total movie length, then copy it down to the last row. Delete any negative (RED) values and any numbers to the right of them, and also delete all values to the right of any death event. Select the ‘Fate Map #1’ tab to view the pre‑formatted fate map. Optionally re‑sort columns (ascending/descending) to group cells by phenotype.

steps.title: Perform statistical analysis of mitotic lengths
steps.instruction: Combine values from columns C (mitosis 1) and E (mitosis 2) to calculate mean mitotic length across generations; generate dot‑plots and assess significance using software such as GraphPad Prism or PlotsofData. Similarly, calculate total cell‑cycle length by plotting all Interphase #2 values. Additional graphs can be created to address specific biological questions (e.g., mother‑daughter comparisons).
